text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected — service=rope-infer-prod; symptom=KV cache cardinality spike + continuous-batching backpressure; severity=sev2. Pager routed to oncall. Root TS=1782123456.

alice: ack, I'm on it. Tailing logs and pulling recent metrics.

bob: seeing continuous_batch_queue length jump ~3x since 02:01 UTC. KV cache size at 98% with high eviction churn. A lot of long-context (NTK/YaRN) requests creating many unique KV keys. p95 latency climbing.

carol_oncall: adding runbook tag; increasing debug for cache module to capture key shapes. Also temporarily throttling the longctx route (route: /v1/generate/long) to reduce new key churn.

bob: sample logs:
```
2026-03-15T02:04:23Z rope-infer[pid=1428]: KVCache.evictions=5243, KVCache.size=98%, continuous_batch_q=128, p99_latency=2200ms, errors=12/5m
2026-03-15T02:05:11Z rope-infer[pid=1430]: request id=abc123 len=2450 ntk=10240 route=/v1/generate/long
```

carol_oncall: recommended immediate mitigation: reduce continuous_batch_max_items + shorter sliding window for KV prefix retention. Proposed hotfix:
```
# hotfix config snippet
continuous_batch_max_items: 64   # from 256
continuous_batch_max_tokens: 4096   # from 16384
kv_cache_window_ms: 30000   # from 60000
kv_prefix_ttl_ms: 120000    # keep short-lived prefix entries
```
Apply to canary (2 nodes) first.

dave_sre: starting canary deploy now (canary=rope-canary-02). Command I'm running:
```
./deploy --service rope-runtime --env prod --image rope-runtime:2026.03.15-hotfix --set continuous_batch_max_items=64 --set kv_cache_window_ms=30000
```
Watching memory/eviction metrics. Will hold if error rate > 1% above baseline.

emily_support: customer impact update — CS notified: acme-corp and beta-saas reported higher latencies and intermittent 503s between 02:03-02:10 UTC. Impact approx 5-10% of requests for those tenants. We're preparing a short status note: "Experiencing degradation on long-context workloads; mitigation in progress."

frank_engineering: quick suggestion — add a guard to rope-scaling: if unique KV key creation rate > X keys/min for longctx requests, fail-fast or degrade to truncated prefix hashing. Also consider per-tenant prefix caps to avoid noisy neighbors.

alice: can we add heatmap sample of KV key cardinality by tenant? That will help root cause if a single tenant is responsible.

bob: extracted top keys; looks like 2 tenants responsible for ~70% of new key space (acme-corp + beta-saas). Keys show full-document hashes instead of sliding-window prefixes — likely a recent client change sending full contexts.

carol_oncall: can we throttle those tenants specifically? If yes, do that as temporary mitigation while hotfix rolls.

dave_sre: applied tenant-specific rate-limits for acme-corp and beta-saas at 02:18 UTC. Canary is stable for 4m, p99 down from 2200ms -> 420ms on canary nodes, overall evictions down 60%. Proceeding to full roll.

frank_engineering: creating a backlog ticket for adding prefix-cutoff heuristics to rope runtime + monitoring alert for KV key churn.

emily_support: sent customer note: "We applied mitigations and rolled a hotfix; you'll see improved latency. We're following up with a postmortem and recommended client-side changes."

carol_oncall: handing off at 02:32 UTC to bob (I need to jump to infra meeting). Full context in thread.

bob: taking over. will monitor for 30m and start postmortem draft.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Hotfix rolled to 100% at 02:46 UTC. Observed metrics: global eviction rate down 72%, continuous_batch_queue < 16 steady, p99 latency trending to baseline. Incident marked RESOLVED. Please file postmortem and include tenant-level data + recommended client changes.

alice: noted. Postmortem owners: bob (lead), frank (engineer on guard logic), carol_oncall (operational timeline).

emily_support: we'll send follow-up outbound to impacted customers with a summary + recommended client patch for using sliding-window prefixes.

frank_engineering: RFC will include: prefix normalization, per-tenant prefix caps, improved metrics (unique-key-rate), and a simulation harness for NTK/YaRN workloads.

carol_oncall: adding incident labels: kv-cache, continuous-batching, long-context, tenant-noisy-neighbor.

bob: thanks team. Postmortem draft ETA EOD.
